cluster_headline: איך נרכשו מאות דירות להשכרה בהנחה של 20%? קרנות הדיור רוכשות עשרות דירות

outlets.headline: איך נרכשו מאות דירות להשכרה בהנחה של 20%? קרנת הדיור רוכשות עשרות דירות, מה היתרונות לשוכרים מכך?

primary_source_search_status: partial — the program was identified through secondary financial press (TheMarker 2026-06-17 and 2026-09-09, Calcalist Aug 2026, nadlancenter). These are bulk purchases of unsold developer inventory by Israeli residential REITs (Rent It, Abu Family, Megureit, among others), not a government program. The fund filings (TASE/Maya immediate reports) were not reached, and the Mako article body could not be fetched. The search index lists the same Mako URL under a different title: 'מי רוכש המוני דירות להשכרה ארוכת טווח - ולמה לא נהנה מזה?'

claims.verified_source_figure: TheMarker, 2026-06-17: Israeli residential REITs bought 422 apartments for about NIS 1.1bn since the start of 2026, mostly unsold inventory from stuck developers. A nadlancenter summary puts the four funds' 2026 deals at more than NIS 1bn.
claims.note: 'Hundreds' matches the aggregate across all residential REITs for the year so far (422 by mid-June, likely more by October). The headline does not say this is an aggregate across several funds. That is a framing gap, not a numeric error.

claims.verified_source_figure: Individual deals: Rent It bought 30 apartments from Beit Yerushalmi for about NIS 63.2m (TheMarker, 2026-09-09). Abu Family is buying 50 units in Netanya from Azorim for NIS 120m (Calcalist, Aug 2026).
claims.note: 'Dozens' describes the size of each deal (30 and 50 units). The 'hundreds vs dozens' mismatch inside the headline is loose wording that mixes the aggregate (hundreds) with the per-deal size (dozens). The numbers do not contradict each other. Minor typo in the headline: 'קרנת' should be 'קרנות'.

claims.verified_source_figure: Discounts reported per deal: Rent It/Beit Yerushalmi 'more than 10%' (TheMarker). Abu Family/Azorim '15%-20%' compared with similar units sold in the same project (Calcalist). An Azorim Living executive estimates that the full benefit package, including tax benefits such as 0.5% purchase tax vs 8%, is worth about 20-25%. That is a different measure from the purchase discount.
claims.note: 20% is a real figure, but it is the top of the range in one 50-unit deal. The headline applies it to 'hundreds' of apartments. Other deals were reported at a discount of more than 10%. No source found shows hundreds of apartments bought at a flat 20%. The article body was not fetched, so it may qualify this as 'up to' or 'about'.
